commands.notes: Offline suites compile standalone Swift executables. Cross-repo protocol parity requires an explicit iOS file path via scripts/check-remote-protocol-parity.sh. No package manager or linter. Meeting core tests use Python standard library; optional model dependencies live in an isolated ignored build environment.

patterns: Record using pinned AVCaptureSession; upload only after recording finalizes.
Main-thread UI and callback state changes.
Groq whisper-large-v3 plain JSON with language from user settings.
Copy before paste; local dictation never sends Return.
Per-job settings and session/request IDs prevent late completions from changing a later dictation.
Recorder stays busy through file finalization, including cancellation.
Local output validates the captured focus target; clipboard fallback is a successful delivery, not confirmed paste.
Local verified corrections settle before a six-second nonactivating opt-out prompt with pointer-hover pause; only a still-valid unchanged correction is automatically added.
Only confirmed enabled vocabulary enters bounded transcription prompts. Prompt use does not imply recognition accuracy.
Neko floating panel never becomes key or main; eye actions call the existing dictation coordinator.
Visual metering treats unknown/silent audio as zero, separately from conservative silence-auto-stop policy.
Voice HUD is compact and anchored top-center or bottom-center; desktop companion placement is a separate design.
Neko introduction is persisted once per user, independent of build versions; ordinary eye hover is color-only with accessibility labels and no tooltips.
Menu bar uses an 18-point fixed-black vector cat in all dictation states; transparent glyphs and accessibility names preserve status and relay distinctions.
Automatic learning starts its opt-out countdown only after the nonactivating bubble passes visibility checks; invisible notices cannot commit vocabulary.
The start-recording guidance button appears only in first-use or explicitly requested onboarding; ordinary HUD previews remain cat-only, and updates preserve the seen flag.
Clipboard history retains ten local text entries; local and remote output share a direct copy hook, while history recovery only copies and never sends paste/submit.
naming: Stable tw.panh.FreeVoiceType bundle ID and Keychain tw.panh.FreeVoiceType.groq / api-key.
User-visible product name: What's up my neighbor. Reuse existing black-cat assets.
error_handling: Report errors via AppKit UI; retain failed audio briefly for explicit retry.
logging: Never log keys, recordings, transcripts or clipboard contents.
tests: Compile offline Swift executable suites using scripts/test-*.sh.

Keep pairing transport and explicit remote-only submit path; validate before paste and submit.

evidence.fact: Text/language rules are isolated Foundation modules.
Remote execution validates identity and target expiry.
Public build compiles flat Swift directory and ad-hoc signs.
AppKit controller composes services; the entry point only launches the application.
Dictation owns bounded retries, settings snapshot, cancellation and recording retention.
Local and remote insertion share clipboard-first output; local dictation uses compatible text-role/window identity checks while remote retains strict validation.
CI executes offline suites before building.
Vocabulary keeps legacy IDs/revisions/tombstones and uses separate persistent learning records.
Local verified paste starts bounded correction monitoring; copied-only output does not.
Independent local meeting research exports time-aligned anonymous transcripts and a manual-name editor, without altering the Mac app.
Controlled Chinese experiments reveal short alternating turns collapse two speakers into one.
Non-activating AppKit HUD uses the selected raster asset and real metering, with fixed cancel/finish eye buttons.
Focused HUD tests cover quiet/missing signal, reduced motion, focus invariants and action gates.
Six-second opt-out vocabulary learning pauses on pointer hover, revalidates the focused bounded range before adding, cancels stale edits, and preserves existing candidates.
Clipboard history uses bounded local persistence and metadata-first polling; native menu recovery does not activate another app or post keyboard events.
